messages.subject: Rstan 2.5 update problem
parts:
Hi,

I just tried updating to Rstan 2.5:

source('http://mc-stan.org/rstan/install.R', echo=T, max.deparse.length=2000)                                                                                                                                
install_rstan()



Whatever I do I can't avoid a segfault when I call into log_prob():

> lp <- log_prob(fit, unconstrain_pars(fit, init.chain()))

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x1150c38, cause 'invalid permissions'

Traceback:
 1: .External(list(name = "CppMethod__invoke_notvoid", address = <pointer: 0x15da510>,     dll = list(name = "Rcpp", path = "/home/john/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0/Rcpp/libs/Rcpp.so",         dynamicLookup = TRUE, handle = <pointer: 0x496cd10>,         info = <pointer: 0x7f0b508a93e0>), numParameters = -1L),     <pointer: 0x60e78e0>, <pointer: 0x5e97ef0>, .pointer, ...)

 7: eval(ei, envir)
 8: withVisible(eval(ei, envir))

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace
Selection:


I've tried removing Rcpp, inline, BH, RcppEigen and rstan before following the 2.5.0 installation instructions and it doesn't help. I did notice new packages are being installed in

~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0/

and there were some older packages in

~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/2.15/

which I removed but that didn't help either. Has anyone got any other ideas I can try? Perhaps i should try to go back to 2.14.

Thanks, John.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Rstan 2.5 update problem
parts:
On Sunday, October 26, 2014 5:29:21 AM UTC-4, John Reid wrote:
Whatever I do I can't avoid a segfault when I call into log_prob():
After you install rstan 2.5, try restarting R before trying to use it.
Has anyone got any other ideas I can try? Perhaps i should try to go back to 2.14.

Was anything R related installed with elevated privileges?  RStan or more specifically Rcpp won't work with R < 3.0. You would probably have better success going forward to R 3.1.x.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Rstan 2.5 update problem
parts:
I can't replicate it, but as long as you are using Linux it shouldn't be too hard to track down with gdb.
  1. From a shell, execute
    R -d gdb --vanilla
  2. In the gdb environment execute
    run
  3. In the R environment, execute
    library(rstan); set_cppo("debug")
  4. Execute the code that causes the crash, which should dump you back into gdb, at which point execute
    bt
If you can paste that whole backtrace into a post, we can probably figure out what the problem is. Be sure to execute
set_cppo("fast")
at some point in the future once the problem is resolved.

Ben
